questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature was crucial as I wanted to explore Canada and its surroundings in my free time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the best experience, however, Canada is really expensive in cost of living!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arriving at UBC it was super easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were student guides present when moving in at campus to help me find the right place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several options for housing on campus, which is also the cheapest one in my experience. Housing was fine and it was easy to apply through the university.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were a kitchen, however you would need to equip it yourself. Meal plans were available, but I did not have that.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is super nice and a great way to meet new people as you live with several roommates.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: This was super easy once you learn how to work Workday out. Here it was super easy to register for courses and drop courses!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are friendly advisors in case you need it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my first priorities!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just to try something out you might find interesting as it is possible to drop courses once you started them in the beginning!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had four 300 level courses. Some were quite easy going compared to UCPH, but this was only nice. Others were very like at home, but the exams themselves were way easier and chill than at UCPH. However, be prepared for assignments and midterms and weekly quizzes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I really liked the style of teaching at UBC because of the teachers were more invested in their students, and we got feedback on all our work, which makes it way easier to actually learn. There were also weekly office hours. On the other hand, the teachers do attendance that will weigh in on your final grade, and here I prefer UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLI_V 327 (3.0) European Integration 
POLI_V 333C (3.0) Issues in Comparative Politics
POLI_V 338B (3.0) Politics and Development 
POLI_V 369K (3.0) Issues in International Security

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend European Integration because of prof. Hübner who is a great teacher and really nice. Also, if looking for a course more flexible, then Politics and Development was super interesting and an online course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was really unexpected that it would be so expensive to buy groceries! My monthly budget was really high because of a lot of traveling and trips!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Way more expensive!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is really cheap to do sports and there is a great aquatic centre for swimming that is free for students!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all sorts of sports, sports facilities, a lot of clubs and activities! There were SO many, and one for each taste.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some of the clubs! Also, attend the bars!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking around British Columbia and go skiing!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People are so friendly and helpful- this made it super easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly met exchange students and the social life here was incredible!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Living with a super christian girl...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are the sweetest!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Prioritise experiences
2. Groceries are expensive 
3. The students are the best

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nope.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friendships and learning a lot!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the tests!

questions.answer: Yes
